9:30 am local: The equation is simple as we enter Day 4 if the Rawalpindi Test. Sri Lanka's lead is 82 and they have just one second innings wicket left. Their only hope of extending this lead is Milan Rathnayake. The bowling all-rounder batter very positively yesterday and raised his 2nd Test half-century. How many more runs can he add today? Pakistan have a history of being poor chasers in the 4th innings, but the visitors will need nothing short of a miracle to win this Test. We will get to know in a couple of hours.

Pitch Report | Aamer Sohail & Salman Butt: It's bright, it's sunny, and it's day four of the Test match. Pitches used in Test matches here usually peak on day three. Yeah, they become very good for batting, and then on day four they start to deteriorate for the spinners to come into play. But I don't see anything changing here. It actually becomes very firm, and it's going to be very good for batting. Yes, with a lot of grass on the pitch, you will see some seam movement, but manageable. Odd ball will keep low, but in my opinion this pitch has been done.
J.D. Silva: "Can Pakistan collapse chasing anything above 100?" That would be too Pakistan a thing to do, even for Pakistan, especially with the pitch still being so good for batting.

Alright, we are ready to roll! How long can Sri Lanka's last pair hold on, and how much further can they stretch the lead? Milan Priyanath Rathnayake has looked really good so far and will be keen to add another 30-40 runs to the total.
